G-F081.trick: EPI = on top of everything (whole muscle), PERI = around a bundle (fascicle), ENDO = inside, on each fiber.
G-F081.tip: Wrap order from outside in: epimysium → perimysium → endomysium. Match the size of what's wrapped.

G-F082.trick: SARCO-MERE = muscle (sarco) part (mere): the smallest repeating unit that contracts, Z line to Z line.
G-F082.tip: The sarcomere is the functional unit of contraction. Its repeating pattern makes the striations.

G-F083.trick: ACh = "Activate Contraction, hey!" It's the go signal at every skeletal neuromuscular junction.
G-F083.tip: Skeletal muscle is always triggered by acetylcholine binding nicotinic receptors on the motor end plate.

G-F084.trick: Calcium is the key: it turns the TROPONIN lock, and the TROPOMYOSIN chain slides off actin's sites.
G-F084.tip: Order matters: Ca2+ binds troponin → tropomyosin moves → myosin binds actin.

G-F085.trick: ATP = the "let go" button for myosin. No ATP = rigor mortis (stuck grip).
G-F085.tip: People often think ATP only powers the pull. Its binding is also what releases the myosin head.

G-F086.trick: ISO-METRIC = same (iso) length (metric). Pushing a wall: lots of effort, no movement.
G-F086.tip: Isometric = tension, no length change. Isotonic = length changes and the load moves.

G-F087.trick: Creatine phosphate = a phone's emergency battery pack: instant recharge, but it runs out in seconds.
G-F087.tip: Order of energy use: stored ATP → creatine phosphate (seconds) → anaerobic glycolysis → aerobic respiration.

G-F088.trick: Vessel walls squeeze with SMOOTH muscle: no stripes, no voluntary control.
G-F088.tip: Involuntary + hollow organ or vessel wall + nonstriated = smooth muscle.

G-F089.trick: ANTAGONIST = the opponent: biceps bends, triceps straightens.
G-F089.tip: Prime mover (agonist) does the action; the antagonist does the opposite; synergists help.

G-F090.trick: TENDON Ties muscle to bone ("T for tie"). Ligament links bone to bone.
G-F090.tip: Muscle pull reaches the bone through a tendon. Don't confuse it with a ligament.

C-ch9-overview.trick: Skeletal fibers = long cables with many nuclei pushed to the sides, plus stripes.
C-ch9-overview.tip: Striated + many peripheral nuclei = skeletal. Striated + one nucleus + intercalated discs = cardiac. No stripes = smooth.

C-ch9-structure.trick: PERImysium = the PERImeter around each bundle (fascicle).
C-ch9-structure.tip: Bundle = fascicle = perimysium. Whole muscle = epimysium. Single fiber = endomysium.

C-ch9-fiber.trick: The A band stays the sAme length. The I band and H zone shrInk.
C-ch9-fiber.tip: Filaments slide; they don't shorten. So the A band (thick-filament length) never changes.

C-ch9-nmj.trick: AChE = the ACh Eraser. Block the eraser and the message keeps shouting "contract!"
C-ch9-nmj.tip: Organophosphate insecticides block acetylcholinesterase, causing continuous stimulation (twitching, spasm).

C-ch9-contraction.trick: Nerve → Tubules → Calcium → Pull: "Never Take Candy, Please."
C-ch9-contraction.tip: For sequence questions, start with the trigger (the nerve releasing ACh) and end with the result (the pull).

C-ch9-energy.trick: Oxygen debt = paying back the oxygen "loan" you took out while sprinting.
C-ch9-energy.tip: Heavy breathing after exercise repays oxygen debt: clearing lactic acid and rebuilding ATP and creatine phosphate.

C-ch9-responses.trick: Holding still under load = ISOMETRIC (same length, no motion).
C-ch9-responses.tip: If nothing moves but the muscle is working hard, the contraction is isometric.

C-ch9-disorders.trick: Use it or lose it: no use = atrophy (shrinking fibers).
C-ch9-disorders.tip: Disuse atrophy shrinks fibers. Muscle fibers don't disappear; they get smaller with fewer mitochondria and capillaries.

C-ch9-smooth-cardiac.trick: Cardiac = striped + involuntary + intercalated discs ("the heart's handshakes").
C-ch9-smooth-cardiac.tip: Intercalated discs are unique to cardiac muscle. They let the heart beat as one unit.

C-ch9-actions.trick: Triceps straightens (the agonist); biceps relaxes and opposes, so it's the antagonist.
C-ch9-actions.tip: The antagonist is the muscle that does the opposite of the movement described.

C-ch9-naming.trick: Read muscle names like a label: ACTION + LOCATION + SIZE (extensor / digitorum / longus).
C-ch9-naming.tip: Muscle names give clues: action (flexor), location (femoris), size (maximus), shape (deltoid), direction (rectus).

C-ch9-head.trick: FRONTALIS = the FRONT of the head: raises eyebrows in surprise.
C-ch9-head.tip: Facial expression muscles are supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII). Damage causes one-sided weakness.

C-ch9-arm.trick: DELToid = Delta-shaped shoulder cap that lifts the arm out to the side (abduction).
C-ch9-arm.tip: Arm out to the side = abduction = deltoid. Pulling it back down = latissimus dorsi and pectoralis major.

C-ch9-trunk.trick: TRANSversus runs TRANSverse (side to side) like a corset, deepest layer.
C-ch9-trunk.tip: From superficial to deep: external oblique → internal oblique → transversus abdominis.

C-ch9-leg.trick: Hamstrings hang on the back of the thigh and bend the knee (flex) like pulling your heel to your butt.
C-ch9-leg.tip: Posterior thigh = hamstrings = knee flexion. Anterior thigh = quadriceps = knee extension.
